items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891; Story 4 names Gideon Vose as founding president.
Gives 'paid by butterfat test, not by milk weight' but never says the test of the station where he delivers governs (second bolded element).
'the provision that made the coming discrepancy a matter of money rather than pride.'
Only Hobart Sill named in Section A; Effie Loomis absent, Teague as bookkeeper not in Section A.
Section A gives Selby as Gideon's son and manager by 1919 but no 1913 start; D3 asserts 1911 (deducted separately).
Story 8 cites 'the ledger's own "station gain" entries' as corroboration; bolded element present, though shape and 1898 origin are not described.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, opened 4 May 1896, on Larrow Green's borrowed glass.
Only the short charge and graduated neck are described; nothing on intake weighing, composite samples or shipping the cream.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., line items, $77.93.
Story 2: 'the Hollow's year-round 0.19-point gap', set against a winter-only hay effect.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie b. 1861, tester from 1896, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Keddie's own book / 'the station's own test book' named; routine not described (unbolded).
3.61 is given but no 1896 average of 3.80 appears in Section A; both figures are required.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. 3.80 not given, but the core fact is there.
Married Orra Brant, whose brother Emmet farmed the largest place on Hessel Bottom (her 1868 birth year is deducted).
1919 circular present; Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent.
Died February 1934.
Six Hessel Bottom farms; Emmet Brant's the largest; wet pasture.
Brant's private weigh book mentioned ('matching') but no 1 January 1897 start.

1902 complaint present, but C1(b) rejects Falke's 3.78-3.61=0.17 'as a minor arithmetic slip, in favor of ... 0.19'. That runs the Hollow-vs-Green gap together with the true shortfall, which the gate says loses the item.
Grigg committee sampled January-March 1908; hay reported as the committee's conclusion.
Brant's 1910 figures (200,000 lb, 3.42) appear only in Section C; proportional loss not stated.
No Roy Brant custody or 1958 loan to Ivy.
Section A mentions only 'the Alder Corners cheese factory'; no Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
No four patrons hauling in the summer flush from 1915.
Only 'independent tests' plus the artifact; fewer than two of the four independence elements.
No 0.19-higher comparison across sixteen seasons in Section A.
Section A never says the same milk tested differently in two buildings.
Rosalie Cudd absent from Section A.
Strawn named for the Ordell circuit, but Story 4 dates his visits 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23); 1907-1936 not given.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
Never says Strawn recorded no figure for the deficiency.
Order 28 June and reply 2 July are right, but the average is given as 'about 3.85 from 1924 onward'.
Station loft present; notebooks to the college library in 1947 absent.
Petition January 1925.
Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two at the station itself.
Watering, skimming by Keddie and wet hay argued; 'no cause established'.
Four exhibits listed, but nothing says Strawn's 1923 notebook contained the answer and was read for other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no cause established; $3,800 'without admission' on 4 May (account is A7.6's aspect).
No one-fifth of $19,000 and no charge to the station-gain account in Section A.
Granddaughter, graduate student at Farland, worked with Leland Vaught.
Section A credits Ivy's 'single measurement', with others supplying the corroborating records; never says she assembled records that had never been in one room.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
Gives mean delivery of 16.27 c.c. (NT-1), not 16.72; no 0.88 or 0.95.
No 95 percent / 3.61-for-3.80 statement in Section A.
Only a bare 76,000 lb in Section A; no 40M lb, no $19,000, no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 24 years after his death; crate forgotten 35 years.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy's father (r18), plus r22's correction.
Second cousins, derived through first cousins Duncan and Roy.
Says full vs half siblings is unresolved and doesn't change the answer; E18's lean still declines to decide.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rumor rejected.
Gideon wrote the by-laws; Selby had a stake in the payment-by-test system his father built.
Asserts 'No genuine kinship.'
Treats the family denial as outranking the rumor; never says no document either way.
Computes 16.27/17.6 = 0.9244, then takes ~5% from the ledger; never 16.72/17.6 = 0.95.
$19,600 and ~19%; key is $19,000 and one fifth.
$90 at 25 cents, stated as the period average and not a 1910 price, with the working shown; meets the alternate acceptance.
Denominators named, but gives 75,810 lb, 5.25% and 4.99%; key is 76,000, 5.26% and 5.00%.
$77.93 by summing the line items.
72 pipettes, but short 1.33 c.c. (from 16.27), not 0.88.
26 years 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898-1922, part years excluded.
Abstention item A02: answers 'Approximately 1,100,000 lb' (Kyle's figure) as the headline.
The variable is the measuring instrument / borrowed measure.
Herds, pasture and season, tester, procedure.
'Rose' and 'fell back' only; no 3.80 or 3.61.
Instrument, not cows, hay or honesty; limit: no mechanism, no size of the error.
1911 interval (r22/r24), ledger surplus (r12/r23), Alder Corners (r10).
Argues the three are independent; 1911 and Alder Corners hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09: asserts 'no', on Kyle's word.
He believed the Hollow's tests were wrong enough to send the 1919 circular.
Only signing the ledger sheets and the 1919 circular are valid; manager start given as 1911; no hearing advocacy, no 'never names the glass'.
Abstention item A03: verdict 'Vose most likely did not consciously know'; no declared inability to settle it.
$3,800 vs $3,500 by majority; condemnation 12 June via the 28 June order; award year 1925 via the diary.
NT-10 (1898 in r11/r23, broken by diary/invoice); NT-14 ($77.39 in r19/r20, broken by arithmetic); NT-16 (eleven in r12/r19).
A04, A06 and A10 not addressed as unsettleable conflicts.
r15's 'whole of 1908' against its own reprinted report (E15).
Cause given as 16.27 c.c. and cessation as a rise to 3.85; never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80 from 16.72.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus (cream heavy), the 1911 interval and Alder Corners.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter vs a flat 0.19, and by Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07: 'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware.'
Abstention item A05: asserts he believed it was 'something in the glass' from 1911.
About 139 words.
Only four series identifiable (ledgers, inspector's notebooks, cheese factory results, 1958 measurement).
No decoy asserted and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
About 5%, 1897, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named; covers both ends.
